title: Do sovereign citizens' claims have any legal basis? | WTFAQ | ABC TV + iview
summary: ABC Australia explainer with a former magistrate: sovereign-citizen consent, living-person and travelling arguments have never succeeded in any Australian court.

assertions.quote: it's not true that a law doesn't apply to you if you don't consent to it
nowhere in any Court have any of these arguments ever succeeded
all of those testimonials are either false or the reported decisions simply don't exist

verdicts.note: Researchers who check claimed wins find none on the theory; apparent wins are dismissals on ordinary grounds or unverifiable.

assertions.quote: can I as a living person do whatever I want of course not
the difference between driving and traveling is unknown in any Australian law
pay money for a script about how they should deal with police officers
